subject: Unit economics follow-up: token volumes & pricing targets
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechx.com>
Cc: dev.patel@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Unit economics follow-up: token volumes & pricing targets

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and a few open items so we can align pricing and a unit-economics model: 

1) Use case & features
- Conversational support for customer service + a summarization feature for compliance logs. Summaries will be invoked on ~10% of sessions as a paid feature.

2) Volume estimates (your ranges from the call)
- Baseline: ~500k tokens/day (avg)
- Peak day: up to ~2M tokens/day
- Monthly: ~15M tokens/month (baseline) with spikes to ~60M in busy months

3) Budget / target cost
- You mentioned a target budget range of $20k–$40k/month and a desired target of ~$50–$80 per 1M tokens for inference alone.

4) Unit economics asks we need from you
- Exact split of free vs paid feature invocations (approx % of sessions that will be charged)
- Expected MAU/DAU for the chat assistants (helps with CAC payback calc)

Next steps I propose:
- We’ll run a short unit-econ model that maps your token profiles to a target $/1M token range and show impact of batching, KV caching, and quantization choices.
- Dev will add estimated latency/quality trade-offs for the model variants we discussed (gpt-small-llm / gpt-medium-llm).

If you can confirm the % paid-feature usage and an expected MAU number, we’ll send a short modeling workbook and a preliminary pricing estimate.

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0123
Redwood Inference — production-grade LLM inference

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechx.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Unit economics follow-up: token volumes & pricing targets

Couple of notes from a runtime/ops perspective — attaching a quick modeling workbook (unit_econ_modeling.xlsx) with assumptions.

- Model choices: gpt-medium-llm provides a reasonable quality/cost tradeoff for summarization + chat; gpt-small-llm can reduce inference cost ~35% but with measurable drop in summary fidelity.
- Batching & KV caching: Effective batching (even modest batch sizes) and prefix KV caching can reduce per-token CPU/GPU utilization by ~20–30% for your workload profile.
- Reserved vs hosted: For steady baseline (~500k tokens/day) a dedicated pool with commit can move your $/1M closer to the $40–$50 range assuming 12–18 month commit; hosted pay-as-you-go is ~20–40% higher at those volumes.
- Margin impact: If your monetization target is $100 revenue per 1M tokens, keeping inference cost under $50/1M gives ~50% gross margin before other infra costs.

Attachment: unit_econ_modeling.xlsx (workbook with scenarios: baseline, peak, reserved vs hosted)

I’ll annotate the workbook with sensitivity to batch size and quantization level. Happy to hop on a quick call if you want to walk through the calc.

— Dev
Head of Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwoodinference.com

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechx.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@fintechx.com>, dev.patel@redwoodinference.com
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 09:28:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Unit economics follow-up: token volumes & pricing targets

Thanks Marissa and Dev — useful recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Volumes: baseline 500k/day average is correct; peaks up to 2M/day during big campaign windows. Monthly baseline ~15M, peaks ~60M as you noted.
- Paid feature split: we expect ~12% of sessions to call the paid summarization feature initially (ramp to ~18% over 6 months).
- MAU: expected initial MAU 40k with goal to ramp to 120k in 9–12 months.
- Budget: Finance has greenlit $30k/month for initial production with the option to expand after Q2.

Two items we care about in the model:
1) Target $/1M tokens we should be aiming to hit to maintain product margin targets (~$150 ARPU per paid user): what gross margin do you recommend vs inference cost?
2) CAC payback: we need a simple table showing CAC payback in months across pricing tiers (we’ll provide CAC targets shortly).

If you can send the modeled $/1M token ranges (hosted vs reserved), a simple CAC payback example tied to $/1M tokens, and a short summary deck, we’ll review with finance next week.

Appreciate it — can we target a deep-dive call Tuesday (2/24) to walk the model?

— Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Product | FintechX
